Strait of Hormuz Status: October 13, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
13 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.57 + 1.66 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 UKMTO reports three vessels struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz; no major wire in this feed carries this independently.

02 GreekReporter.com reports a tanker has been hit in the Strait of Hormuz, reported on October 12; Al Jazeera reports India has condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the region.

03 Brent stood at $105.57 as of 06:10 UTC, up 1.66% over 24 hours; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to normal commercial traffic, with vessel strikes continuing at a sustained pace. UKMTO reports three vessels were struck by unknown projectiles in the strait; no major wire in this feed carries this independently. Separately, GreekReporter.com reports a tanker has been hit in the strait, reported on October 12, and Al Jazeera reports India has condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the region. OnlineKhabar English News also reports two oil tankers were attacked in the strait, with two Indian sailors missing. The IRGC claims it struck a third supertanker, per The Economic Times and ANI News, a claim no maritime authority has confirmed. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the feed's 84 headlines indexed in the past 24 hours reflect a heavily active news cycle, though several rows typically represent a single story. Brent stood at $105.57 as of 06:10 UTC, up 1.66% over 24 hours, with WTI at $92.56. As of 06:22 UTC, 67 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
